paras: The police shooting of James Jackson took place in Chicago on or about July 30, 1920, when detective-bureau sergeants shot the 22-year-old as he tried to get away from them. Jackson was left in critical condition in the County hospital, and two of the city's Black weeklies, the Chicago Whip and the Chicago Defender, reported the shooting in their police columns.

Jackson lived at 2716 Dearborn Street, and the Whip described him as "alleged to have been wanted for the commission of a crime," without naming the offense. According to the Defender, two sergeants of the detective bureau came to serve a warrant on him.

The Whip reported that Jackson was arrested on July 30 by "Sgts. Six and Starks," attempted to escape, and was shot by the officers. The Defender's account named the officers as Sergeants Scott and Stark and said Jackson broke away and ran when the warrant was served. In that version Scott first fired in the air to frighten him, and when Jackson ran faster, "Scott aimed. Jackson fell."

As of August 7 the Whip described Jackson as in critical condition, and the Defender placed him in the County hospital. No later report of whether he survived, of an inquiry into the shooting, or of the charge against him appears in the coverage.

Both reports appeared on August 7, 1920, as short items in columns of local police, court and hospital news. The Whip's item ran under the heading "Vacation in Chicago Leads to Jail" among accounts of stabbings, family quarrels and accidents, and repeated the officers' explanation that Jackson "attempted to escape." The Defender's "In the Grip of the Law" column gave the sharper narrative, telling the warning shot and the aimed shot in clipped sentences, but likewise offered no comment on the use of force. No report of the shooting was found in the white press.

The two papers agree on a sergeant named Starks or Stark of the detective bureau but differ on his partner, "Six" in the Whip and Scott in the Defender; the same Whip column mentions a "Sergeant Scott of the bureau" in another item. They also differ on whether Jackson was already under arrest when he fled and on whether one officer or both fired.
